**Tenement** is an American three piece rock band from Appleton, Wisconsin, United States, formed in 2006. They are often associated with the American hardcore punk scene.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-2) Their recorded output has been described as everything from "noise pop" to "fuzz punk",[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-4) while in a live setting, they are often known for experimentation, improvisation, and high-energy performance.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-6) The visual art of singer/guitarist Amos Pitsch is associated with most of their records, as well as several records by other notable punk and hardcore bands.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-7) In January 2013, _NME_ included Tenement in their "rising stars of 2013".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-8)_CMJ_ called Tenement a "breakout artist to watch" in 2014.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-9) In 2015, Tenement was included in _Spin_ 's "The 50 Best Rock Bands Right Now".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-10) In 2016, they were included in _Rolling Stone_ 's "10 Great Modern Punk Bands".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-11)

Tenement and their relation to contemporary punk, hardcore, and DIY was the subject of _The New York Times_ ' June 2015 Popcast; which was hosted by author Ben Ratliff and featured special guests Maria Sherman and Liz Pelly. In reference to Tenement and the DIY scene in which they operate out of, Pelly noted, "It's pretty clear that for these musicians punk is more something they relate to on an ideological level."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-12)
In 2016, Tenement was invited to play _Eaux Claires_, an outdoor music festival curated by Justin Vernon of Bon Iver and Aaron Dessner of The National. "A Frightening Place For Normal People," from their 2015 double album _Predatory Headlights_, was included on the festival's teaser mixtape as a remix called "A Frightening Place For Normal People And Farmers" and credited to Tenement and radio host Jack Raymond.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-13) Rock Of The Arts said of their festival appearance, "(...) Pitsch and Tenement really exhibit the independent qualities that Eaux Claires holds so dearly. An underground basement band from Appleton, Wisconsin, that continues to proudly fly the DIY flag, never forgetting where they came from no matter how much attention they receive."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-14) Speaking on the eclectic nature of the festival's lineup, Justin Vernon told _Billboard_: "For me it's so interesting, and it's part of the uniqueness of our situation at Eaux Claires, that Erykah Badu and Tenement -- there might be an equal amount of fans for Erykah Badu and Tenement at this thing. And while Erykah is an extremely important part of the landscape of this year, everything plays into that. For me it's just interesting to watch those worlds interact and also coexist simultaneously." [[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-15)

Actor and comedian Chris Gethard curated a playlist for Brooklyn, New York club Shea Stadium in 2016, compiling his favorite performances at the venue. He included Tenement's 2013 performance of "Spit In The Wind" with the note, "Simply put, they don't make 'em better than Tenement. My wife is significantly cooler than I am and was the one who made it clear to me that Tenement would be one of my favorite bands, and she was totally correct."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-16)

## Style and reputation
[edit]
For most of their formative years, members of Tenement lived in and operated the BFG punk house in Appleton, Wisconsin- which hosted hundreds of bands over the course of eight years and served as a recording space for portions of each of their studio albums from 2011 to 2015. Their connection to the house and the relationships they developed with national touring artists that played there cemented their reputation as disciples of DIY culture.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-18) Despite national acclaim, the house (and the band) remained an underground fixture within the confines of the city of Appleton. Pitsch told _The Post-Crescent_ in 2015, "We've been an enigma to people and in our own little world".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-19) The same year, he told _Ghettoblaster Magazine_, "In a town like Appleton, Wisconsin, a place like BFG was a lawless jungle. I’d always thought that it was meant to be bulldozed and not to be handed over to new tenants. The energy that place held after we’d been there for eight years wasn’t meant to linger in a normal family environment."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-20) For many, setting foot in The BFG was an experience that brought them to a closer understanding of what drove Tenement as a group and how they fit- personally and creatively- into the greater scheme of music and art in America. Some saw them as off-the-grid, insular, outlying personas, and others saw them as music savants, students of their record collections, and eccentrics with nearly singular-interest personalities. _RVA Mag_ visited the house in 2010 and wrote: "[Amos'] room, located on the top floor of the BFG House, Appleton’s main house show venue, is indicative of his lifestyle. Some recording equipment is set up on a desk, with a computer that doesn’t connect to the internet.

# Tenement Members, Gear & Sound
## About
**Tenement** is an indie punk and power pop band originating from Appleton, Wisconsin. Formed in 2006, the group is known for its catchy yet intelligent approach to punk music, blending sharp melodies with a willingness to experiment. The band is led by **Amos Pitsch (vocals, guitar)**, who is also notable for his striking collage artwork that adorns the band's releases. Pitsch is joined by **Jesse Ponkamo (bass)**, whom he met in high school, and **Eric Mayer (drums)**, who became a permanent member after initially joining as a temporary replacement. Tenement's discography includes albums like _Napalm Dream_ and _Predatory Headlights_, showcasing their dynamic range and lyrical depth.

# Tenement Members, Gear & Sound
## How to Sound Like Tenement
Tenement’s sound is characterized by its gritty and energetic punk aesthetic, balanced with melodic power pop sensibilities. Their sonic palette is aggressive yet accessible, marked by **crunchy guitar riffs** that often utilize overdrive pedals for a raw, biting tone. The **bass lines are punchy and driving**, providing a solid backbone that complements the frenetic guitar work. Drumming in Tenement’s music is both forceful and dynamic, adding to their high-energy performances. To capture their sound, musicians might focus on utilizing **simple but effective effects** like overdrive and distortion, paired with **high-gain tube amplifiers** to achieve that classic punk intensity. The band's recordings also exhibit a DIY ethos, with production that maintains a live, raw feel — an approach that aspiring musicians can emulate with straightforward recording techniques and minimal post-processing.

# Tenement Members, Gear & Sound
## About
**Tenement** is an indie punk and power pop band originating from Appleton, Wisconsin. Formed in 2006, the group is known for its catchy yet intelligent approach to punk music, blending sharp melodies with a willingness to experiment. The band is led by **Amos Pitsch (vocals, guitar)**, who is also notable for his striking collage artwork that adorns the band's releases. Pitsch is joined by **Jesse Ponkamo (bass)**, whom he met in high school, and **Eric Mayer (drums)**, who became a permanent member after initially joining as a temporary replacement. Tenement's discography includes albums like _Napalm Dream_ and _Predatory Headlights_, showcasing their dynamic range and lyrical depth.

# Tenement Members, Gear & Sound
## How to Sound Like Tenement
Tenement’s sound is characterized by its gritty and energetic punk aesthetic, balanced with melodic power pop sensibilities. Their sonic palette is aggressive yet accessible, marked by **crunchy guitar riffs** that often utilize overdrive pedals for a raw, biting tone. The **bass lines are punchy and driving**, providing a solid backbone that complements the frenetic guitar work. Drumming in Tenement’s music is both forceful and dynamic, adding to their high-energy performances. To capture their sound, musicians might focus on utilizing **simple but effective effects** like overdrive and distortion, paired with **high-gain tube amplifiers** to achieve that classic punk intensity. The band's recordings also exhibit a DIY ethos, with production that maintains a live, raw feel — an approach that aspiring musicians can emulate with straightforward recording techniques and minimal post-processing.

texts.1: **Tenement** is an American three piece rock band from Appleton, Wisconsin, United States, formed in 2006. They are often associated with the American hardcore punk scene.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-2) Their recorded output has been described as everything from "noise pop" to "fuzz punk",[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-4) while in a live setting, they are often known for experimentation, improvisation, and high-energy performance.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-6) The visual art of singer/guitarist Amos Pitsch is associated with most of their records, as well as several records by other notable punk and hardcore bands.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-7) In January 2013, _NME_ included Tenement in their "rising stars of 2013".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-8)_CMJ_ called Tenement a "breakout artist to watch" in 2014.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-9) In 2015, Tenement was included in _Spin_ 's "The 50 Best Rock Bands Right Now".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-10) In 2016, they were included in _Rolling Stone_ 's "10 Great Modern Punk Bands".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-11)

Tenement and their relation to contemporary punk, hardcore, and DIY was the subject of _The New York Times_ ' June 2015 Popcast; which was hosted by author Ben Ratliff and featured special guests Maria Sherman and Liz Pelly. In reference to Tenement and the DIY scene in which they operate out of, Pelly noted, "It's pretty clear that for these musicians punk is more something they relate to on an ideological level."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-12)
In 2016, Tenement was invited to play _Eaux Claires_, an outdoor music festival curated by Justin Vernon of Bon Iver and Aaron Dessner of The National. "A Frightening Place For Normal People," from their 2015 double album _Predatory Headlights_, was included on the festival's teaser mixtape as a remix called "A Frightening Place For Normal People And Farmers" and credited to Tenement and radio host Jack Raymond.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-13) Rock Of The Arts said of their festival appearance, "(...) Pitsch and Tenement really exhibit the independent qualities that Eaux Claires holds so dearly. An underground basement band from Appleton, Wisconsin, that continues to proudly fly the DIY flag, never forgetting where they came from no matter how much attention they receive."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-14) Speaking on the eclectic nature of the festival's lineup, Justin Vernon told _Billboard_: "For me it's so interesting, and it's part of the uniqueness of our situation at Eaux Claires, that Erykah Badu and Tenement -- there might be an equal amount of fans for Erykah Badu and Tenement at this thing. And while Erykah is an extremely important part of the landscape of this year, everything plays into that. For me it's just interesting to watch those worlds interact and also coexist simultaneously." [[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-15)

## Style and reputation
[edit]
For most of their formative years, members of Tenement lived in and operated the BFG punk house in Appleton, Wisconsin- which hosted hundreds of bands over the course of eight years and served as a recording space for portions of each of their studio albums from 2011 to 2015. Their connection to the house and the relationships they developed with national touring artists that played there cemented their reputation as disciples of DIY culture.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-18) Despite national acclaim, the house (and the band) remained an underground fixture within the confines of the city of Appleton. Pitsch told _The Post-Crescent_ in 2015, "We've been an enigma to people and in our own little world".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-19) The same year, he told _Ghettoblaster Magazine_, "In a town like Appleton, Wisconsin, a place like BFG was a lawless jungle. I’d always thought that it was meant to be bulldozed and not to be handed over to new tenants. The energy that place held after we’d been there for eight years wasn’t meant to linger in a normal family environment."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement_(band)#cite_note-20) For many, setting foot in The BFG was an experience that brought them to a closer understanding of what drove Tenement as a group and how they fit- personally and creatively- into the greater scheme of music and art in America. **Outagamie County** ( _OW-tə-GAY-mee_)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-1) is a county in the Fox Cities region of the U.S. state of Wisconsin, in the northeast of the state. As of the 2020 census, the population was 190,705.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-2020-census-55087-2) Its county seat is Appleton.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-GR6-3)

Outagamie County is part of the Appleton Metropolitan Statistical Area, which is itself part of the Appleton-Neenah-OshkoshCombined Statistical Area. It was named for the historic Meskwaki (Fox) people.
"Outagamie", a French transliteration of the Anishinaabe term for the Meskwaki (Fox) people, means "dwellers of the other shore" or "dwellers on the other side of the stream",[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-4) referring to their historic habitation along the St. Lawrence River and south of the Great Lakes. They occupied considerable territory in Wisconsin before colonization.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-5) Outagamie County was created in 1851 and organized in 1852.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-6) Before that, it was under the jurisdiction of Brown County.
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has an area of 645 square miles (1,670 km 2), of which 638 square miles (1,650 km 2) is land and 7.1 square miles (18 km 2) (1.1%) is water.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-GR1-7)

*   Shawano County - north  
*   Brown County - east

*   Wolf River - The Wolf River runs through the city of New London and the village of Shiocton along western half of the county.  
*   Fox River - The Fox River follows the southeastern corner of the county, running through the cities of Appleton and Kaukauna  
*   Shioc River - This river runs merges with the Wolf River in the village of Shiocton.  
*   Embarrass River - The Embarrass River runs through the city of New London and merges with the Wolf River there.

*   Black Otter Lake - Located in Hortonville, it receives much recreational use by anglers as the county's only lake.
Outagamie County's government consists of an elected County Board of Supervisors, a County Executive, and 36 county agencies and departments.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-outagamie.org-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-9)
The county executive serves as its chief executive officer, participating in the legislative process with the County Board of Supervisors and exercising administrative authority and control over the county's operations, departments, offices, boards, programs, and communications.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-10)
Department heads are appointed by the county executive, subject to the approval of the board of supervisors. The county executive also appoints members to the county's boards and commissions. The county executive sets the annual budget in consultation with and subject to the approval of the board of supervisors.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-11)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-outagamie.org-8)
County Executive Tom Nelson was first elected in 2011.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-12)

**Outagamie County** ( _OW-tə-GAY-mee_)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-1) is a county in the Fox Cities region of the U.S. state of Wisconsin, in the northeast of the state. As of the 2020 census, the population was 190,705.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-2020-census-55087-2) Its county seat is Appleton.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-GR6-3)
texts.1:
Outagamie County is part of the Appleton Metropolitan Statistical Area, which is itself part of the Appleton-Neenah-OshkoshCombined Statistical Area. It was named for the historic Meskwaki (Fox) people.
"Outagamie", a French transliteration of the Anishinaabe term for the Meskwaki (Fox) people, means "dwellers of the other shore" or "dwellers on the other side of the stream",[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-4) referring to their historic habitation along the St. Lawrence River and south of the Great Lakes. They occupied considerable territory in Wisconsin before colonization.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-5) Outagamie County was created in 1851 and organized in 1852.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-6) Before that, it was under the jurisdiction of Brown County.
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has an area of 645 square miles (1,670 km 2), of which 638 square miles (1,650 km 2) is land and 7.1 square miles (18 km 2) (1.1%) is water.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-GR1-7)

*   Shioc River - This river runs merges with the Wolf River in the village of Shiocton.

Outagamie County's government consists of an elected County Board of Supervisors, a County Executive, and 36 county agencies and departments.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-outagamie.org-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-9)
The county executive serves as its chief executive officer, participating in the legislative process with the County Board of Supervisors and exercising administrative authority and control over the county's operations, departments, offices, boards, programs, and communications.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-10)
Department heads are appointed by the county executive, subject to the approval of the board of supervisors. The county executive also appoints members to the county's boards and commissions. The county executive sets the annual budget in consultation with and subject to the approval of the board of supervisors.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-11)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outagamie_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-outagamie.org-8)

**Calumet County** is a county located in the U.S. state of Wisconsin. As of the 2020 census, the population was 52,442.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calumet_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-QF-2) The county seat is Chilton.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calumet_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-GR6-3) The county was created in 1836 (then in the Wisconsin Territory) and organized in 1850.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calumet_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-4)
Calumet County is included in the Appleton, WI Metropolitan Statistical Area as well as the Appleton-Oshkosh-Neenah, WI Combined Statistical Area.
The Holyland is partially located in southern Calumet County.
The county's name originated from the word _calumet_, the French name for the ceremonial pipes used by Native Americans in councils on the east shore of Lake Winnebago.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calumet_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-NHHS69-5)
In the 1830s, the United States government relocated Native Americans from New York and New England to the southwest part of the county; these included the Brothertown Indians, Oneida Indians, and Stockbridge-Munsee Indians. This was a second migration for the Brothertown and Stockbridge Indians, who had moved to New York after the American Revolutionary War. The Oneida shared land on their reservation with these peoples, who had been displaced by the years of colonization in New England, warfare and disease.
Many of the early European residents in the Holyland region in the southern part of the county were emigrants from the Schleswig-Holstein region in Germany in the 1840s.
The county was legally organized on February 5, 1850, by Chapter 84 Laws of 1850.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calumet_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-Wulff-6)

Calumet County figures prominently in the 2015 Netflix television series _Making a Murderer_, which documents the arrests and trials of Manitowoc County resident Steven Avery, which involves from 2005 the Calumet sheriff's department and district attorney's office of Ken Kratz.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calumet_County,_Wisconsin#cite_note-7)

The west boundary is largely in Lake Winnebago. The Niagara Escarpment runs north–south several miles east of the western boundary. The topography has been greatly influenced by glaciation.
